newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran inflation 0.8 percent in March.
newsitem.headline: Honduran inflation 0.8 percent in March.

text.p: Consumer prices in Honduras rose 0.8 percent in March, lifting the Central American country's accumulated inflation rate for the year to 5.3 percent, the Central Bank said on Thursday.
It was the lowest monthly inflation rate of the year following 2.0 percent in January and 2.4 percent in February.
The moderated inflation in March was due to the relative strength of the Honduran lempira against the U.S. dollar last month and slight decreases in fuel costs, the Central Bank said.
Lower prices also were registered for kerosene, vegetables, tomatoes and corn, the Central Bank said.
Contributing to upward pressure on consumer prices were increases in health-care costs, tobacco, drinks and household goods.
Year-over-year inflation was 25.8 percent as of March. Inflation was 24.9 percent in 1996.
